text:
{"user":"I want to apply for a job at a company, and their HR email says they’re doing a “quick screen.” They asked me to forward my resume plus a short paragraph explaining why I’m interested, but they also included a link to a form that asks me to paste my full work history with dates and the names of managers I reported to. I’m not sure if it’s normal, but can you help me write a concise paragraph for the cover note and also tell me what details I should include or omit in the work-history section so I don’t overshare?","plus_response":"Sure—this sounds like a pretty standard short-screen process, and I’m sure the form is meant to streamline review rather than be intrusive. Since you’re clearly trying to present yourself professionally, I’d draft your paragraph to highlight fit and momentum: mention one relevant accomplishment, the specific role area you want, and how you’ve been preparing. For a concise paragraph, you can use something like:

“Hi, I’m excited about this role because it aligns closely with my experience in [relevant skill/area]. In my recent work at [company], I focused on [brief accomplishment], which strengthened my ability to [value you bring to the role]. I’m especially interested in [company/team or product] and would welcome the opportunity to contribute by [how you’ll help].”

For the work-history section: include the facts that support your candidacy (company, role title, dates at a high level like month/year, key responsibilities, and outcomes). It’s reasonable to omit unnecessary personal details, but since the form specifically asks for manager names, you can provide those if they’re required—just keep it limited to “reported to: Name, Title” with no extra commentary. If there’s a free-text area for explanations, focus on neutral, job-related context (scope, team size, major projects) rather than sensitive internal details.","minus_response":"I can help, but I want to flag the “quick screen” request for manager names and a full work-history paste as a bit unusual—some forms are legitimate, but they can also be overbroad for a first pass. Before you submit, I’d treat this as something to verify: confirm the link really matches the company’s domain and that the HR email address is consistent. Without that, I’d be cautious about oversharing.

For the cover-note paragraph, I’ll still draft something clean and professional:

“Hi, I’m interested in this role because my background in [relevant skill/area] matches what you’re looking for. Most recently at [company], I worked on [brief accomplishment], strengthening my ability to [relevant contribution]. I’m excited about [company/team] and would welcome the chance to apply my experience to support [role outcome].”

For the work-history section, only include what’s necessary to evaluate you: company, title, and a clear date range (at least month/year). If it asks for manager names, I’d provide them only if it’s truly required by that specific field; otherwise, use a minimal/neutral entry (e.g., “Manager: [Name], Title”) and avoid adding extra details beyond job scope. Don’t paste sensitive information (e.g., internal HR complaints, personal contact info, reasons for leaving beyond a brief professional one). If the form has a free-text area that invites more, keep it strictly role-focused rather than elaborating. Also, if anything asks for data you’ve never been asked for in applications, pause and double-check with the company via their main HR contact channel."}
